title: Riot Platforms Just Became an AI Landlord. The Market Still Isn't Buying It.
subtitle: A 191-megawatt, 20-year lease with a frontier AI lab — reported to be Anthropic — turns a bitcoin miner into a data-center developer.
summary: Riot has stacked nearly $10 billion in contracted data-center revenue in six months, anchored by a lease with a frontier AI lab that Bloomberg reports is Anthropic. The pivot is real — but bitcoin still drives most of the revenue and the company is burning cash.

image.caption: Riot Platforms' Rockdale, Texas campus, where the company is building 191 megawatts of AI data-center capacity under a 20-year lease with a frontier AI lab that Bloomberg reports is Anthropic.

bodyHtml:
For years, Riot Platforms was the purest of pure-play bitcoin miners: ASIC racks, megawatt-hours, and a stock that rose and fell with the price of the coin. In about six months, it quietly became something else — an AI data-center landlord with two of the most significant names in artificial intelligence on long-term leases.

Here's the headline: a build-to-suit lease at Riot's Rockdale, Texas campus for 191 megawatts of critical IT capacity with a 20-year term through June 2048 and roughly $9.1 billion in initial contract revenue. Bloomberg reports the tenant is Anthropic; Riot hasn't confirmed the name. First 96 megawatts go live in December 2027, the rest by June 2028, and two five-year extension options could push the deal toward $16.1 billion.

This didn't come out of nowhere. In January, Riot signed its first data-center deal at the same campus: 25 megawatts for AMD, delivered in phases by May, with another 25 megawatts optioned in April and room to grow to 200. That contract starts around $311 million over ten years and could approach $1 billion with extensions. CEO Jason Les puts the total at 241 megawatts contracted and roughly $9.8 billion in long-term contracted revenue — in about six months.

Now the why. Bitcoin mining is a commodity business with brutal unit economics, and Q2 made that concrete: all-in cost to mine ran about $90,631 per bitcoin against an average production value near $71,667. Mining at current prices is uneconomical, full stop. The AI pivot converts stranded power and land into contracted cash flows backed by investment-grade tenants — a fundamentally better business.

The economics on the new side look dramatically better. Management guides cumulative net operating income of $7.3 to $8.2 billion — $365 to $411 million a year at an 80 to 90 percent NOI margin — against illustrative build capex of $2.1 to $2.3 billion, $11 to $12 million per IT megawatt. Morgan Stanley is funding early construction with a $573 million interim facility while an investment-grade credit backstop is finalized. There's also a $177 million engineering backlog, roughly 90 percent data-center.

The Q2 numbers show the transition. Revenue hit $174.2 million, up 14 percent year over year, but bitcoin mining revenue fell 19 percent to $113.7 million — about 65 percent of the total. Engineering revenue more than tripled to $37.3 million, and data-center added $23.2 million, including $4.9 million of operating-lease revenue at an 84 percent margin. Riot produced 1,587 bitcoin, up 11 percent, but posted a GAAP net loss of $237.2 million, negative adjusted EBITDA, and deeply negative free cash flow.

The market's response has been telling. The stock surged on the announcement, then gave back most of the pop — investors can't decide if this is a miner with a side hustle or a data-center developer in the making. Shares trade well off their highs, and the company's market value sits below its contracted pipeline. That gap is the whole argument.

Now the risks — they're genuine. One lease is roughly $9.1 billion of the $9.8 billion in contracted revenue, so tenant concentration is extreme — if the reported Anthropic deal wobbles, the bull case loses its spine. Execution is the second risk: 191 megawatts of Tier III capacity by 2028 is a different game than racking ASICs, and everyone is fighting for the same gear. Third, bitcoin still drives about 65 percent of revenue while mining is cash-negative — the AI story doesn't erase that drag soon.

Liquidity helps the wait: more than $1.2 billion on hand — roughly 11,380 bitcoin worth about $666 million plus $548.9 million in cash — and no equity issued in Q2. Beyond Rockdale, the Corsicana campus holds a full gigawatt of approved power — about 756 megawatts of potential IT capacity — under a non-binding letter of intent with a single tenant in advanced discussions. If that converts, the story compounds.

Bottom line: this is a real pivot, not a press-release pivot. The market is pricing in meaningful doubt — fair given the execution risk — but it's ignoring that Riot already delivered one buildout on time and on budget, secured financing, and stacked nearly $10 billion in contracted revenue in six months. This is a different company than a year ago. The bitcoin drag is real; so is the upside.

Disclosure: The Signal holds no position in RIOT. Positions may change. This is not financial advice.
